title: Weather alerts
sub: National Weather Service warnings and advisories for where you are, including marine ones like a small craft advisory on the water off your spot. Tap one for the details.

title: Best days ahead
sub: Two weeks rated from bite times, the forecast, alerts, tides and the conditions you catch fish in. Storms, strong wind and alerts mark a day down; the best three are picked out with the reasons.

title: Plan the best day
sub: Tap a day to plan a trip for its best hours, at the place you’re looking at.

title: Your route
sub: While a session runs and the app is open, your route is recorded and saved with it. Keep the app on screen while you move: phones pause web apps in the background.

title: Find a place by name
sub: Type a lake, river, boat launch or town and tap Search. Your saved spots come first, then places from OpenStreetMap, nearest first. Coordinates and map links work too.

title: Named for you
sub: Pick one and the spot gets its place and name. Save it, and catches made there link to it.

title: Search the map
sub: The magnifying glass finds a place on the map: the map moves there, with New spot here and Plan a trip here.

title: Map layers
sub: The layers button adds Washington’s boat ramps, hand launches, fishing piers and shore-fishing sites from WDFW, NOAA nautical charts, and your session routes.

title: Boat launches and access
sub: Tap a launch, pier or shore-fishing site for directions, or save it as a spot or plan a trip there. B is a boat ramp, H a hand launch, P a pier, S shore fishing.

title: NOAA nautical charts
sub: On the water, NOAA’s charts add depths, channels, buoys and hazards – and the orange line is the route from your session. The charts are for planning, not navigation.

title: Import a log
sub: Bring in catches from another app or your own spreadsheet. Settings → Import a log matches the columns by name and shows a preview; catches already in your log are skipped.

title: Check the columns
sub: Change any match, the units and how dates are written. Weather is filled in afterwards for catches with a GPS position, and Undo removes the whole import.

title: Imported
sub: Done – the catches join your log with their place, lure and size.

title: Places from your GPS
sub: GPX, KML and KMZ files from a GPS, fish finder or Google Earth bring their places in as spots. Export spots, catches and routes as GPX from Settings.

title: On Windows
sub: The Windows app installs from one file with no administrator rights, opens in its own window and works offline, maps included. Drop a spreadsheet or GPX file on it to import.
